jobs.occupation: Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
jobs.description:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027.

Title:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments

Research area and project description:
How can grazing management be optimized to benefit both biodiversity and nature-based beef production? This PhD project will address this question through analyses of long-term biodiversity monitoring data, development of digital biodiversity indicators, and field experiments in Danish semi-natural habitats.

Grazing is a key ecological process in many ecosystems. However, biodiversity outcomes depend on how grazing is managed, including grazing intensity and timing. Despite its widespread use as a conservation tool, important knowledge gaps remain regarding which grazing strategies deliver the greatest biodiversity benefits and how these outcomes can be documented in a robust and scalable way.

The PhD project is part of the interdisciplinary Nature&Beef initiative and will combine ecology, biodiversity monitoring, remote sensing and data science. The selected candidate will work with unique datasets from the Danish national biodiversity monitoring programme (NOVANA), field experiments, drone imagery and other digital monitoring approaches.

The project will focus on four interconnected themes:
1) Identifying grazing practices associated with positive biodiversity outcomes using long-term monitoring data.
2) Evaluating the effects of grazing intensity and grazing season on biodiversity in a large-scale field experiment.
3) Developing and validating image-based indicators of vegetation structure and biodiversity condition from field and drone imagery.
4) Contributing to the development of AI-based methods for mapping vegetation and habitat condition from drone images.

The project offers an opportunity to contribute to evidence-based conservation and the development of practical tools that can support land managers, farmers, conservation practitioners and value-chain actors in documenting biodiversity outcomes. The findings will help build a stronger scientific foundation for biodiversity-friendly grazing practices and nature-based beef production.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants to the PhD position must have a Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in biology or equivalent. The applicants have documented experience in botanical surveys including species identification skills of North-European flora. The applicant must have a driver license applicable in Denmark. Demonstrated proficiency in data management and analysis, image analysis, and experience using R.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is C.F. Møllers Allé 8, building 1110, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Senior researcher, head of section Camilla Fløjgaard, e-mail: camf@ecos.au.dk (main supervisor)
 For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
 
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk 
 
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 1 December 2026 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 1 March 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

jobs.occupation: Associate Director - External Data Acquisition Lead (EDAL)
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**The Associate Director, External Data Acquisition Lead (EDAL) role is a clinical data manager with expertise in the data collection of 3rd party data from various external providers (e.g. laboratories, eCOA providers, technology providers, etc.). The EDAL provides a leadership role in the oversight of the external clinical data integration processes as well as oversight of data quality from various external providers performing testing or data collection services on behalf of Genmab. The EDAL serves as the subject matter expert for all external data management activities performed for clinical trial teams. This role provides strategic data management expertise and is accountable for all end-to-end Data Management activities and deliverables pertaining to external data. The employee will provide oversight of external vendors and the data and/or data services they provide to Genmab. The External Data Lead will support the development and optimization of processes and tools to enable success of the Clinical Operations department. The employee will represent Data Management in Operational Committee’s/fora with the partners and/or DM/stat vendors. The employee will support /train colleagues in and advise on handling of external data management related processes/issues and may act as a mentor. Moreover, the employee shall support the overall strategy and development of Data Management by attending/leading task force initiatives within the department and/or as part of cross-departmental teams.

**Responibilites

**

• Lead external data acquisition across one or more studies/programs, ensuring high-quality, timely, analysis-ready data aligned with trial objectives.

• Influence protocol and amendment development by advising on external data collection design, integration feasibility, and alignment with CDASH/SDTM and EDC requirements.

• Lead planning and oversight of external data flow strategies and DTS across diverse data types (PK/ADA, biomarker, imaging, central lab, eCOA/ePRO, PD, IRT, etc.) to ensure compliant integration.

• Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure external data acquisition supports operational and scientific goals.

• Develop and manage Trial Data Integrity Plans (TDIP) and Data Flow

• Create and maintain data transfer specifications (DTS) requirements. Ensure data collection requirements are aligned with external vendor capabilities and vendor data are compatible with the clinical database and SDTM requirements to support data integration, analysis and reporting. Ensure vendor data is transferred in standard data formats.

• Provide thorough review of external vendors budget and change order

• Act as escalation point for complex vendor issues (timeline deviations, integration challenges, misalignment to trial needs).

• Mentor and guide junior External Data Acquisition Leads, providing direction on best practices, issue resolution, and development.

• Lead cross-functional initiatives including SOP development, process improvement, tools optimization, and external data standards governance.

• Partner with procurement/legal/vendor managers to review technical language in contracts and work orders, ensuring alignment with Genmab standards and systems.

• Promote portfolio-level consistency and scalability through training, knowledge sharing, and strategic planning support.

• Mentor and develop team members to ensure consistency of External Data Management practices.

• Ensure External Vendor deliverables are performed in compliance with protocol, ICH, GCP and SOPs

**Requirements

**

• Bachelor’s or Master's degree in a relevant technical area; Master’s degree preferred.

• 10+ years of experience in external or clinical data management, with strong third-party vendor oversight and data acquisition experience.

• Experience working on Oncology trials/data

• Experience designing and governing DTS and complex data flows supporting EDC integration and CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM).

• Strong knowledge of diverse external data types (e.g., biomarker, central lab, imaging, eCOA/ePRO, genomic) and ability to align acquisition strategies to clinical and analytical objectives.

• Experience managing projects, vendors, and process improvements in global environments.

• Proven performance in earlier role.

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$157,360.00---$236,040.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

**About You

**

• You are genuinely passionate about our purpose

• You bring precision and excellence to all that you do

• You believe in our rooted-in-science approach to problem-solving

• You are a generous collaborator who can work in teams with a broad spectrum of backgrounds

• You take pride in enabling the best work of others on the team

• You can grapple with the unknown and be innovative

• You have experience working in a fast-growing, dynamic company (or a strong desire to)

• You work hard and are not afraid to have a little fun while you do so!

**Locations

**Genmab maximizes the efficiency of an agile working environment, when possible, for the betterment of employee work-life balance. Our offices are crafted as open, community-based spaces that work to connect employees while being immersed in our powerful laboratories. Whether you’re in one of our office spaces or working remotely, we thrive on connecting with each other to innovate.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

**Job Description Summary

**The Production Engineer – Calibration & Maintenance is responsible for the calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle management of production, inspection, measurement, and test equipment used in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

The role works closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, equipment owners, and external service providers to ensure equipment remains calibrated, maintained, compliant, and available for production.

Responsibilities include day-to-day calibration and preventive maintenance coordination, HxGN EAM administration, calibration assessments, controlled procedures and work instructions, supplier coordination, and equipment compliance.

This is a hands-on Production Engineering role supporting manufacturing operations across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration/loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

**Job Description

****Roles & Responsibilities

**

• Coordinate the site calibration program, including calibration schedules, call-in activities, equipment status, due dates, and timely completion.

• Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including equipment preparation, shipment, return, documentation review, and release back to production.

• Ensure new, returned, overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment is appropriately assessed and controlled before use.

• Act as SME for calibration and maintenance activities in HxGN EAM, maintaining asset records, calibration setups, preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, task plans, and supporting documentation.

• Perform and support calibration assessments, including equipment requirements, criticality, acceptance criteria, calibration methods, frequencies, and maintenance needs.

• Develop and maintain calibration and maintenance procedures, SOPs, and work instructions in collaboration with equipment owners, SMEs, and Quality.

• Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for production and test equipment while minimizing disruption to manufacturing.

• Support investigations, risk assessments, and product-impact assessments related to overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment, and provide input to NC/INV/CAPA activities where applicable.

• Coordinate external calibration and maintenance suppliers, including quotations, service activities, documentation, and AGORA purchase orders.

• Support internal and external audits by ensuring calibration and maintenance records are complete, traceable, compliant, and audit-ready.

• Monitor calibration and maintenance performance and drive improvements in equipment compliance, availability, data quality, and execution efficiency.

**Required Qualifications

**

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Metrology, Maintenance, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience with calibration, preventive maintenance, equipment management, or Production Engineering in a regulated manufacturing environment.

• Understanding of calibration principles, equipment control, documentation, traceability, and manufacturing process requirements.

• Experience with computerized maintenance or Enterprise Asset Management systems, preferably HxGN EAM or comparable systems.

• Experience working within controlled procedures, work instructions, and change management processes.

• Experience coordinating suppliers, service activities, quotations, and purchase orders.

• Knowledge of GMP and Quality Management System requirements within regulated manufacturing.

**Desired Characteristics

**

• Experience within medical device manufacturing or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.

• Hands-on and practical approach to supporting manufacturing equipment and production operations.

• Structured working style with strong ownership and ability to manage recurring deadlines.

• Strong collaboration skills across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and external suppliers.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfortable balancing equipment compliance, production continuity, quality requirements, and operational priorities.

• Proactive and improvement-focused approach to equipment reliability and calibration/maintenance processes

******Additional Information

******Relocation Assistance Provided: No

The Senior Manager also contributes to the continued development and optimization of Genmab’s global end-to-end labeling processes, systems, and capabilities, helping ensure they remain efficient, scalable, compliant, and aligned with evolving regulatory requirements and industry standards. • Demonstrated ability to manage complex deliverables, priorities, vendors, and timelines in a global, cross-functional environment.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across functions and geographies.

• Knowledge of U.S. labeling requirements is an advantage.

Are you eager to build an international career across our end-to-end Supply Chain, powering renowned dairy brands such as Lurpak, Arla and Castello? Do you want responsibility from day one and the chance to lead strategic projects that shape how we plan, produce and move sustainable dairy? As a Supply Chain Graduate, you will gain broad, hands-on experience across our end-to-end Supply Chain, build a strong international network and accelerate your development towards future leadership roles in Arla.

About the Supply Chain Graduate Programme

The 2-year Supply Chain Graduate Programme offers an end-to-end perspective of Supply Chain with four rotations of 6 months each. You will develop your project leadership skills while gaining hands-on experience in Logistics, Production, Planning and Engineering & Technology. You will work on strategic projects in areas such as sustainability and digitalization and get the full perspective of Arla’s Supply Chain – from farm to fridge. This opportunity lets you explore your leadership potential, accelerating your career towards a leading role in our Global Supply Chain function to help shape the future of sustainable dairy.

We are looking for graduates to join the programme at one of our production sites in Denmark, Sweden, United Kingdom, and Germany. You will spend 18 months at your primary location and have a 6-month rotation abroad during the programme. We will assign you to the local site where we see the best fit for your development opportunities.

As a graduate in Supply Chain, you will be exposed to production sites, distribution centers, and warehouses. You and your fellow Supply Chain graduates will work on strategically important projects at your respective sites, all focusing on the same overall topics - such as sustainability, digitalization and lean optimization, among much more. The rotations are structured as follows:

• First rotation: You will start at an operations site working in either Production or Logistics.

• Second rotation: In your second rotation, you will stay in the same location and work in Planning.

• Third rotation: In this rotation, you will go abroad to a different country and work with a co-graduate in Engineering & Technology.

• Fourth rotation: In the last rotation, you will return to your first location and work in either Production or Logistics.

How you will make an impact as a Supply Chain Graduate

As part of our Supply Chain Graduate Programme, you will receive a variety of development opportunities every step of the way. To ensure your professional and personal development, you will benefit from:

• Real responsibilities from day one enabling on-the-job learning

• Leadership development camps, taking place in different markets with your graduate colleagues

• One-to-one mentoring from senior leaders

• An impactful graduate experience and access to a global graduate network

Across your four rotations you will:

• Lead and deliver projects that improve safety, quality, service, costs and sustainability

• Work with data, digitalization and automation to optimize processes

• Gain an understanding of the full Supply Chain

• Build stakeholder management and change leadership skills in diverse, international teams

Are you our next Supply Chain graduate?

To apply for the Supply Chain Graduate Programme, please ensure that you can tick off the following boxes:

• You are completing or have completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree between September 2025 and September 2027, preferably within supply chain, engineering, food/dairy science, operations, logistics, production or a related field

• You have a strong interest in end-to-end supply chain, processes and operations with general business acumen and commercial interest being an advantage

• Preferably minimum one year of relevant work experience from student jobs or minimum 6 months of internship

• You are globally mobile and willing to go abroad for 6 months during the 2-year programme

• International experience and cross-cultural understanding gained from working, studying or volunteering abroad will be considered a plus

• You are fluent in English. Furthermore, it is an advantage if you speak Danish, German or Swedish

Additionally, we are looking for personal qualifications including:

• 
Clear leadership aspirations and the drive to deliver results

• 
A global, curious mindset with strong relationship-building and influencing skills

• 
Curiosity, openness to change, and resilience with a continuous interest in learning

• 
Humbleness, self-awareness and receptiveness to feedback

Important information before application

The application period for the Supply Chain Graduate Programme runs from November 2nd 2026 to January 3rd 2027. Before applying, please make sure that you have already prepared your CV and cover letter in English. You will be asked different questions on the application page, thus we recommend that you start the application process from a computer instead of a mobile phone.

For additional information, read more about the Supply Chain Graduate Programme on our website. Here, you can get inspiration from some of our previous and current graduates and learn more about the programme. You can also read more about what to expect from the recruitment process.

If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

We are looking for a Payroll Specialist who can ensure stable, accurate, and professional payroll processes, and who thrives in a collaborative environment with a focus on quality and continuous improvement

About the job

As our new Payroll Specialist, you will become part of Group Finance, where you will join a larger team while sharing the primary responsibility for payroll accounting with one colleague. You will primarily be responsible for Danish payroll, and you will also provide support related to international payroll processes in our sales countries, where payroll administration is primarily handled by external payroll providers.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Managing the payroll process from A to Z, from data collection and validation to payment and reconciliation

• Payroll controls, including validation, quality assurance, and the handling of alerts and reports

• Administration of new hires, terminations, absences, holiday accounts, reimbursements, and related payroll activities

• Handling severance payments, holiday pay accruals, and other payroll-related accounting entries

• Payroll reconciliations, including three-way reconciliations between the payroll system, finance, and statutory reporting/eIncome, as well as reconciliations of accrued and outstanding payroll-related balances

• Preparing audit documentation and delivering ad hoc reporting

• Contributing to process optimization and continuous improvement initiatives, including ensuring best practices across payroll processes

You will report to the Director, Group Finance, while working closely with HR Operations.

Who are you?

We are looking for someone who has:

• Experience with payroll systems (SAP Payroll and SAP SuccessFactors are considered an advantage)

• Strong Excel skills and a solid understanding of systems in general. You are comfortable working analytically with large datasets, identifying patterns and connections in data, and applying a strong technical understanding

• A keen eye for detail and a high degree of data accuracy

• Knowledge of payroll legislation and, ideally, collective agreements for blue collar employees

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate professionally with HR, Finance, and employees across the organization, including responding to payroll-related inquiries from employees

• The ability to work independently and take ownership of your responsibilities, while also enjoying close collaboration with a colleague on shared tasks

• A proactive and curious approach to processes, along with a desire to contribute to continuous improvements

• The ability to work in a structured and reliable manner, as our payroll processes require a high level of accuracy and quality

• Fluency in Danish and strong English language skills

Who are we?

In Group Finance, you will become part of a dedicated team focused on quality, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving. In addition to Payroll, the department includes Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Cash and Bank Management, Controlling, as well as process owners and system specialists who work closely together across Finance and other key functions.

The team has an informal and supportive culture, deep professional expertise, and a strong commitment to helping one another while continuously developing and improving processes together.

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of making affordable healthcare accessible.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

Are you passionate about developing advanced microwave oscillator systems for world-class Doppler radar solutions?

At Weibel, you will become part of a growing, technology-driven company where curiosity, innovation, and dedication are the foundation of our global success. We develop and manufacture high-performance radar systems at our in-house production facilities, enabling us to explore new solutions while maintaining uncompromising quality. Our greatest asset is our talented employees, who work in a modern environment and continuously advance our market-leading radar solutions for applications such as air surveillance and precision tracking.

We are strengthening our Antenna R&D Group and are looking for a Senior Microwave Engineer to join us as we enter a new growth phase.

About the position

As our new colleague, you will drive the development of microwave oscillators from early concept through design, integration, and deployment into our radar systems. You will collaborate closely with colleagues across analog, digital, and mechanical engineering disciplines. In addition, you will contribute to architectural improvements in collaboration with our system architects.

Your primary responsibilities include:

• Designing, developing, and optimizing oscillator modules and circuitry for high-performance radar applications.

• Researching and evaluating new oscillator technologies to improve phase noise, frequency stability, and overall system performance.

• Serving as the technical subject-matter expert for oscillator designs and their integration.

• Supporting prototype assembly, testing, and DFM reviews to ensure successful transfer to production.

• Providing technical support to in-house production and customers through engineering guidance, root-cause analysis, and documentation.

This is an exciting opportunity to shape the frequency-generation foundation of Weibel's radar portfolio and enhance the performance of our next-generation radar systems.

About you

You thrive in an Agile environment, where you work both independently and in close collaboration with your team and cross-functional stakeholders. You value continuous learning and are comfortable operating in a dynamic R&D setting with multiple parallel activities, some requiring immediate attention and others progressing through structured project plans.

Your qualifications include:

• An M.Sc. or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field, preferably with a specialization in RF or microwave hardware design.

• Hands-on experience with oscillator and frequency-generation design, e.g., VCOs, DROs, or PLL-based synthesizers, including optimization of phase noise, frequency stability, and spectral purity.

• A strong background in RF, microwave, or mixed-signal systems development, combined with a solid understanding of the full product development lifecycle.

• Familiarity with regulatory requirements (e.g., radio and EMC) and military standards applied in mission-critical industries.

• Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

Furthermore, you are comfortable leveraging AI-assisted tools to improve engineering efficiency and quality.

Your new team

Our team consists of over 10 engaged colleagues, with experience ranging from a few years to more than 35 years in radar engineering. The team is part of our cross-functional Antenna R&D Group, bringing together architects and design specialists across RF, analog, digital, and mechanical domains to deliver cutting-edge radar technology.

You thrive in an environment that requires you to work independently on some tasks and in close collaboration with your colleagues across the entire company on others. • A relevant engineering degree

• 10+ years of experience in system testing of complex integrated HW and SW systems

**About Genmab

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Working closely with operators, tool technicians, maintenance, quality, and product development teams, you will drive process optimization, troubleshoot complex production challenges, validate new products and materials, and implement robust solutions that ensure stable and efficient production.

This role offers the opportunity to combine hands-on engineering, problem-solving, and continuous improvement in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where new technologies, products, and materials are continuously introduced and your will have a direct impact on product quality, process capability, equipment uptime and productivity.

**What You’ll Be Doing

You'll work with advanced injection moulding technologies and play a key role in introducing new products, materials, and manufacturing solutions, while being supported by knowledgeable colleagues who value teamwork, technical excellence, and continuous improvement.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant in Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a fixed-term position as Research Assistant in Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design, is open for appointment from January 1, 2027, or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is 2 years.

Your work tasks
Your work will include developing, training and evaluating machine-learning models based on circuit data, board geometries, simulation results and design images. You will develop surrogate models that approximate thermal and electromagnetic solvers, enabling faster evaluation of design alternatives. The position may also involve computer vision for recognizing circuit structures, component placements and printed circuit board geometries from photographs or other images. In addition, you will investigate graph-based methods for representing circuit relationships, evaluating design rules and generating or testing hypotheses for circuit designs. You will contribute to the development and verification of agentic workflows, where artificial intelligence systems combine models, tools and design rules to reason through and support electronics design tasks. You will prepare datasets, document computational workflows, validate model performance and share results with colleagues working in artificial intelligence, power electronics, semiconductors and software development.

The position is offered within the research field of Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design and contributes to AAU Energy’s focus areas of Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence, and Energy Efficiency in Components and Systems. The Research Assistant will be affiliated with the Section of Power Electronics System Integration and Materials.

Your competencies
You have a relevant master’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, electronics, artificial intelligence or a related field, and you are interested in working at the intersection of machine learning and power electronics design. You have a solid foundation in applied machine learning. Familiarity with electronic systems, including printed circuit boards, circuit topologies, components and the physical principles that influence electrical, thermal and electromagnetic performance, will help you engage with the engineering context of the role.

You have practical experience developing, training and evaluating machine-learning models, and you can translate complex engineering challenges into data-driven methods suited to a research environment. You are comfortable working with structured and unstructured engineering data, including circuit representations, board geometries, simulation data and images. Experience with computer vision, graph-based machine learning or graph neural networks will support your work with methods that interpret circuit layouts and geometries, reason about relationships between components, and generate or assess design hypotheses.

You are interested in developing surrogate models that approximate thermal and electromagnetic simulation tools while maintaining sufficient accuracy for use in electronics-design workflows. You work systematically with model validation, data quality and reproducible experiments, and you understand that artificial intelligence methods for engineering need to be technically robust as well as useful to domain specialists.

You communicate clearly in English, both in writing and dialogue, and you work well in a multidisciplinary environment where colleagues with expertise in artificial intelligence, power electronics and software development collaborate closely. You take responsibility for your tasks, ask constructive questions when assumptions need clarification, and contribute with curiosity and sound technical judgement to the development of new methods for intelligent electronic-system design.

Who we are
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements 
Appointment as a research assistant requires academic qualifications at master's degree level.

How to apply  
Your application must include the following: 

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position. 
• Curriculum Vitae (CV). 
• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and potential PhD diploma). 
• Documentation of teaching qualifications (optional). 
• Additional qualifications in relation to the position. 
• References/recommendations. 
You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society. 

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment. 

Do you have any questions? 
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.    

Selected candidates will be invited for an interview. Interviews are expected to be held during December 2026

Further information 
Read more about our recruitment process here   

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Research assistant”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
